ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the vertical axis is U/V, and the horizontal axis is I/A. The U-I characteristic straight lines of two resistors both start from the origin. The straight line marked Ra is steeper than the straight line marked Rb. The dashed auxiliary lines in the figure show that when I = 2 A, the voltage corresponding to Ra is about 20 V, and the voltage corresponding to Rb is about 10 V. Then reason: in the U-I graph of a resistor, the slope R = U/I. From the figure, Ra = 20/2 = 10 Ω, Rb = 10/2 = 5 Ω, so Ra is greater than Rb.
